title: Introduce subnet ownership tagging and marshalled DNS fallback for multi-account control plane
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Teams running private control planes in shared AWS/Transit setups needed safer, auditable subnet allocation and a resilient DNS handoff when Route53 conditional forwarding or cross-account resolver rules are delayed. This PR provides two coordinated changes: 1) a subnet ownership tagging scheme plus terraform helpers so the installer can claim/verify subnets deterministically without clobbering other teams' allocations; 2) a marshalled DNS fallback that wires a short-lived resolver forwarder (Route53Resolver + lambda-backed conditional rules) to ensure control plane name resolution remains available during cross-account propagation windows.

What changed (high level):
- Added a new Terraform module modules/subnet/ownership.tf to standardize owner-tag, purpose-tag, lifecycle-tag and an idempotent claim flow (lookup by tag -> create if absent -> return allocation).
- Refactored modules/network/outputs.tf to expose subnet-owner metadata and tag filters used by downstream modules (endpoints, NAT, route53).
- Implemented modules/dns/marshalled_forwarder.tf: optional resource set (aws_route53_resolver_rule + aws_lambda + IAM) which creates a short TTL forwarder that is automatically removed after a configurable window.
- Added an installer helm values.yaml flag (helm/installer/values.yaml) enableFeature.subnetOwnership and enableFeature.dnsFallback with sensible defaults for private deployments.
- Added scripts/upgrade-hook.sh and helm hooks that run a pre-upgrade claim step and post-upgrade teardown of temporary resolver resources.
- Tests: new integration test scenario tests/integration/subnet-ownership.yaml and unit helpers tests for tag matching.

Compatibility notes: The DNS fallback is opt-in and off by default. It is intended for cross-account Route53 setups where resolver propagation latency has caused transient control-plane failures. Subnet ownership tagging follows the existing tag namespace (k: redwood:env, redwood:team) but introduces redwood:subnet-owner and redwood:subnet-purpose keys — these are non-breaking for existing installs.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module with docs and examples
- [x] Helm value toggles and hooks
- [x] Integration test scenario for CI
- [x] Security review for lambda IAM role (minimal privileges)
- [x] Migration notes in docs/README-deployments.md

Commits summary: [1/5] modules: add subnet ownership module with claim/lookup pattern; [2/5] dns: add marshalled Route53 resolver + lambda forwarder; [3/5] helm: expose toggles and add pre/post-upgrade hooks; [4/5] scripts: upgrade-hook.sh + teardown helper; [5/5] tests: add integration scenario and unit tests.

Files changed (high level): modules/subnet/ownership.tf, modules/subnet/README.md, modules/network/outputs.tf, modules/dns/marshalled_forwarder.tf, helm/installer/values.yaml, scripts/upgrade-hook.sh, tests/integration/subnet-ownership.yaml, docs/README-deployments.md.

CI: First CI run failed on terratest flakiness in us-west-2; flaky test quarantined and re-run. After fixes, all checks pass (terraform fmt, validate, terratest integration, helm lint, unit).

Merge rationale: Enables safer private control plane rollouts across multi-account setups and reduces incident surface caused by DNS propagation delays. Backward compatible and feature-flagged.
